mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the FEDFUNDS rate above 4% in the month prior to the decision is associated with a near-term negative S&P 500 20-day forward return due to expectations of tighter policy compressing equity discount rates.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS crosses above 4% in the prior month
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not statistically different from zero during the tightening month (p > 0.05), or FEDFUNDS does not cross the 4% threshold.

mechanism_narrative: Rising monthly PAYEMS (labor market strength) coinciding with UNRATE below 7% predicts a positive S&P 500 60-day forward return as strong labor demand supports corporate earnings growth.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases while UNRATE < 7% in the current month
failure_condition: Rank IC of the interaction < 0.05 over the 60-day horizon, or 60-day returns are not statistically positive (p > 0.05) during the defined labor signal.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly surge in GDPC1 (goods demand) exceeding 10% year-over-year in the prior quarter is associated with a positive S&P 20-day forward return as it anticipates sustained economic momentum.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 quarterly YoY growth > 10% in the prior quarter
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not positive during the signal (p > 0.05), or GDPC1 growth is not above 10%.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly decline in INDPRO (industrial production) exceeding 5% suggests supply-side weakness, predicting a negative S&P 5-day forward return as investors anticipate softer earnings.
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are not negative in at least 70% of INDPRO < -5% events (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When FEDFUNDS remains below 2% for three consecutive months, the S&P 20-day forward return is predicted to be positive, reflecting expectations of lower policy constraints and easier financing for equities.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS < 2% for three consecutive months (current and prior two)
failure_condition: 20-day returns are not statistically positive during the three-month FEDFUNDS < 2% window (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in HOUST (housing starts) and PAYEMS (labor) above their 12-month moving averages predicts a positive S&P 60-day forward return as both indicators suggest economic expansion.
candidate_trigger: HOUST > 12-month MA and PAYEMS > 12-month MA in the current month
failure_condition: Rank IC of the interaction < 0.1 over 60 days, or 60-day returns are not significantly positive (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp drop in RSAFS (retail sales) below 100 million dollars in the current month, while UNRATE remains above 8%, signals weak consumer demand and predicts a negative S&P 20-day forward return.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS < 100 and UNRATE > 8% in the current month
failure_condition: 20-day returns are not negative when the signal is active (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When CPIAUCSL (CPI) increases by more than 0.5% month-over-month and UNRATE is below 6%, it indicates persistent inflation pressures without tight labor, predicting a negative S&P 20-day forward return.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL MoM % > 0.5 and UNRATE < 6% in the current month
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not negative during the defined inflation signal (p > 0.05).
